After playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]], he was selected with the fourth overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. Evans went on to win the 2010 [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]]. He was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in 2013 before being traded back to the Kings in 2017. After successive stints with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and [[Indiana Pacers]], Evans, who would have become a free agent at the end of the 2019 season, was dismissed and disqualified from the NBA in May for violating the terms of the league's anti-drug program, but was reinstated in February 2022. ==High school career== Tyreke Evans was born in [[Chester, Pennsylvania]], where he was chiefly raised by his three older brothers.Jere Longman. "[https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/21/sports/ncaabasketball/21preps.html Prep Star's Rise Aided by His Brother's Best Intentions]". ''[[New York Times]]''. February 21, 2008. Retrieved on June 25, 2008. For high school, Evans attended American Christian Academy in [[Aston, Pennsylvania]].{{cite magazine |title=Get To Know: Tyreke Evans |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2010/10/18/18get-to-know-tyreke-evans |magazine=Sports Illustrated |access-date=December 28, 2022 |date=October 18, 2010}} There, he quickly proved an impressive talent on the basketball court, and by his sophomore season, began drawing comparisons to no less than Hall of Famer [[Tracy McGrady]].Mark Beech and Ted Keith. "[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/magazine/06/26/where.will.they.be0703/index.html Where Will They Be?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070519171329/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2006/magazine/06/26/where.will.they.be0703/index.html |date=2007-05-19 }}" ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''. June 27, 2006. Retrieved on June 25, 2008. In his senior campaign, he put up averages of 32.1 points, 8.8 rebounds, 5.7 assists, and 4.3 steals per game.{{cite web |author=12  Tyreke Evans |url=http://www.gotigersgo.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/evans_tyreke00.html |title=Player Bio: Tyreke Evans – MEMPHIS OFFICIAL ATHLETIC SITE |publisher=Gotigersgo.com |date=1989-09-19 |access-date=2012-01-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307060812/http://www.gotigersgo.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/evans_tyreke00.html |archive-date=2012-03-07 }} He was selected as the MVP of the [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's High School All-American Game]] and, together with [[Brandon Jennings]], was named co-MVP of the [[Jordan Brand Classic]]. He was also named to the first-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]. He was featured in the documentary ''[[Gunnin' for That No. 1 Spot|Gunning for That #1 Spot]]'' directed by [[Adam Yauch|Adam "MCA" Yauch]] of the [[Beastie Boys]] when he was only sixteen years of age.[https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0946888/ Adam Yauch – IMDb] Evans was chosen to be the keeper of the ''[[SLAM Magazine|Slam]]'' High School Diary for the 2008 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2009/03/evans-almighty/ |title=Evans Almighty |publisher=Slam Online |date=2009-03-02 |access-date=2012-01-15}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Evans was listed as the No. 3 point guard and the No. 6 player in the nation in 2008.[https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tyreke-Evans-38381;_ylt=Aq9AVd1GVt1YYby81N77xz9GPZB4 Tyreke Evans Recruiting Profile] ==College career== In April 2008, after also considering [[Villanova University]] and the [[University of Texas]], Evans announced his commitment to the [[Memphis Tigers]]."[http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=400780 Tyreke Evans picks Memphis Tigers] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080620121631/http://www.sportingnews.com/yourturn/viewtopic.php?t=400780 |date=2008-06-20 }}". [[Associated Press]]. ''[[The Sporting News]]''. April 16, 2008. Retrieved on June 25, 2008. After playing [[small forward]] throughout high school, Evans initially struggled with his transition to [[shooting guard]] at Memphis. But as soon as coach [[John Calipari]] had him start at the [[point guard]] position for the eleventh game of the season, Evans flourished in a 60–45 win over [[University of Cincinnati|Cincinnati]]; he played 33 minutes and tallied 14 points, 10 rebounds, and 8 assists, the latter two being season highs. With Evans at the helm, Memphis would not lose another game until the [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], falling to the [[Missouri Tigers]].{{cite web|last=Wolken |first=Dan |url=http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/dec/29/tigers-take-down-bearcats-60-45-despite-cold-start/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081231143325/http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/dec/29/tigers-take-down-bearcats-60-45-despite-cold-start/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=2008-12-31 |title=Tigers take down Bearcats, 60-45 |publisher=Commercialappeal.com |access-date=2012-01-15}} Evans won [[Conference USA]] Rookie of the Week as many as eight times.http://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2009/feb/09/lucky-7-conference-usa-honors-tigers-evans-seventh/?feedback=1#comments {{dead link|date=January 2012}} He was also the only freshman among the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]]'s 2009 finalists for the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy|National Player of the Year]] award that is named in honor of [[Oscar Robertson]]. ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2009–2013)=== ==== 2009–10: Rookie of the Year ==== On March 31, 2009, Evans declared himself eligible for the [[2009 NBA draft]], opting to forgo his remaining three seasons of collegiate eligibility. He was selected on June 25, 2009, by the [[Sacramento Kings]] with the fourth overall pick. On December 1, 2009, Evans was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Month|Western Conference Rookie of the Month]] for games played from the beginning of the season through November.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/evans_named_western_conference_2009_12_01.html |title=Sacramento Kings – Home |work=Nba.com |date=2009-12-01 |access-date=2012-01-15}} Over that period, he put up averages of 18.8 points, 5 rebounds, 4.7 assists, and 1.3 steals in 36.1 minutes per game. Also notably, on December 21, he led the Kings back from a 35-point deficit to defeat the [[Chicago Bulls]] 102–98;{{cite web|author=United Center, Chicago|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291221004 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091228003904/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291221004 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 28, 2009 |title=Kings rally from 35 down to clip Bulls at finish |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2009-12-21 |access-date=2012-01-15}} by scoring 9 of the Kings' last 11 points, he single-handedly outscored the Bulls in the fourth quarter, with his 11 points besting the Bulls' 10 points scored. [[File:Tyreke Evans Dec 2012.jpg|thumb|right|Evans with the Kings in December 2012]] On January 4, 2010, Evans was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for the second month straight.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2010/news/01/04/rookies.ofthe.month/index.html |title=NBA.com |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=2010-01-04 |access-date=2012-01-15 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100105042511/http://www.nba.com/2010/news/01/04/rookies.ofthe.month/index.html |archive-date=2010-01-05 }} On February 12, Evans won the 2010 [[Rising Stars Challenge|Rookie and Sophomore Game]] MVP award after recording 26 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists, and 5 steals on 11-of-15 shooting. In an act of sportsmanship, Evans opted to share the award with [[DeJuan Blair]], who had put up 22 points and pulled down 23 rebounds. In a victory over the [[Toronto Raptors]] on March 11, Evans recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with his 19 points to go along with 10 assists and as many rebounds.[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/362062-kings-rookie-tyreke-evans-records-first-triple-double-in-sacramento Sacramento Kings Rookie Tyreke Evans Records First Triple-Double] Evans became just the fourth rookie in NBA history to average at least 20 points, 5 rebounds, and 5 assists after [[Oscar Robertson]] (1960–61), [[Michael Jordan]] (1984–85), and [[LeBron James]] (2003–04).{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/goal_accomplished_2010_04_12.html |title=Sacramento Kings – Home |work=Nba.com |date=2010-04-12 |access-date=2012-01-15}} On April 27, 2010, Evans was recognized for his accomplishments by being awarded the 2009–10 [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] Award.{{cite web|last=Associated |first=The |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/04/30/sports/basketball/30sportsbriefs-rookie.html |title=Kings' Evans Is Rookie of Year |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=2010-04-30 |access-date=2012-01-15}} ==== 2010–13: Later seasons ==== On December 29, 2010, [[O. J. Mayo]] hit an off-balance shot to put the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] up by one point with only seconds remaining in the game; with no timeouts left, [[DeMarcus Cousins]] inbounded the ball to Evans, who dribbled to half court and nailed a three-pointer to secure a two-point win for Sacramento. Though it came in a loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]], Evans tallied a then career-high 35 points to go along with 5 rebounds, 3 assists, and 3 steals on January 21, 2011. He later missed 19 regular season games on account of [[plantar fasciitis]] in his left foot and thus did not play in that year's NBA Rookie Challenge. On November 24, 2011, Evans agreed to a deal to play for [[Virtus Roma]] in Italy during the NBA lockout; the deal had an NBA out-clause allowing him to return to the Sacramento Kings when the lockout ceased.[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/89005/virtus-roma-officially-announces-tyreke-evans.html Virtus Roma officially announces Tyreke Evans] In December, he returned to the Kings after the [[2011 NBA lockout]] had ended. On January 28, 2012, he scored a season-high 31 points in a 96–93 loss to the Utah Jazz.[https://web.archive.org/web/20120129173525/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320128026 Jazz fend off Kings as Jimmer Fredette misses potential game winner] In [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13]], Evans missed 16 out of 20 games between November 30 and January 5 due to a left knee injury. He finished the season with averages of 15.2 points and 4.4 rebounds per game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/e/evansty01/gamelog/2013/ Tyreke Evans 2012-13 Game Log] ===New Orleans Pelicans (2013–2017)=== [[File:Tyreke Evans Trevor Ariza.jpg|thumb|left|Evans with the Pelicans in February 2014, being defended by [[Trevor Ariza]].]] Evans was acquired by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] on July 10, 2013, in a sign-and-trade deal involving three teams; the deal sent [[Robin Lopez]] to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and [[Greivis Vásquez]] to the Kings.{{cite web|title=NEW ORLEANS PELICANS ACQUIRE TYREKE EVANS AND JEFF WITHEY IN THREE-TEAM TRADE|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-tyreke-evans-and-jeff-withey-three-team-trade|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=July 23, 2013}} On December 30 that year, Evans hit the game-clinching shot with 1.2 seconds remaining in a victory over the Trail Blazers.[http://www.nba.com/games/20131230/PORNOP/gameinfo.html Notebook: Pelicans 110, Trail Blazers 108] On April 14, 2014, he scored a career-high 41 points during a 101–89 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140414/OKCNOP/gameinfo.html |title=Notebook: Pelicans 101, Thunder 89 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-04-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150105055634/http://www.nba.com/games/20140414/OKCNOP/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-01-05 |url-status=dead }} In a 101–95 win over his former team, the Sacramento Kings, Evans tallied a near triple-double with 19 points, 12 rebounds, and 9 assists.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150403/NOPSAC/gameinfo.html |title=Pelicans beat Kings 101-95, gain ground in playoff race |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-04-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150407025032/http://www.nba.com/games/20150403/NOPSAC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-04-07 |url-status=dead }} On December 1, 2015, he played his first game of the 2015–16 season after having missed the Pelicans' first 17 games while recovering from right knee surgery. In 31 minutes as a starter, Evans recorded 20 points and 10 assists in the loss to the Memphis Grizzlies.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151201/MEMNOP/gameinfo.html |title=Gasol's 38 points lead Grizzlies past Pelicans 113-104 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-12-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225035717/http://www.nba.com/games/20151201/MEMNOP/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2017-12-25 |url-status=dead }} On the 11th of that same month, he scored 27 points and hit a career-high 5 three-pointers in a 105–103 win versus the [[Washington Wizards]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20151211/WASNOP/gameinfo.html Evans scores 27 points, Pelicans beat Wizards 107-105] On February 11, 2016, he underwent another round of surgery to his right knee and was ruled out for the rest of the season.[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/tyreke-evans-undergoes-successful-surgery-1 Tyreke Evans Undergoes Successful Surgery] On December 15, 2016, being his first game since January 25, Evans played 11 minutes and posted 7 points, 3 rebounds, and 2 assists during a 102–95 victory over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899827|title=Davis, Hield lift Pelicans past Pacers, 102-95|work=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}} On January 12, 2017, Evans scored a season-high 29 points in a 104–95 victory over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900007|title=Pelicans, minus Davis, hand Nets 8th straight loss, 104-95|work=ESPN.com|date=January 12, 2017|access-date=January 13, 2017}} ===Return to Sacramento (2017)=== On February 20, 2017, Evans was traded along with [[Buddy Hield]], [[Langston Galloway]], and 2017 first and second round draft picks to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[DeMarcus Cousins]] and [[Omri Casspi]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-hield-evans-galloway|title=Kings Acquire Hield, Evans, Galloway, and 2017 Draft Selections|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2017|access-date=February 20, 2017}} Three days later, in his first game for the Kings since 2013, Evans scored 15 points off the bench in a 116–100 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900261|title=Cauley-Stein scores 29, Kings beat Nuggets 116-100|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}} On March 8, 2017, he scored a season-high 26 points in a 114–104 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900352|title=Ginobili, Lee lead Spurs by Kings in Leonard's absence|work=ESPN.com|date=March 8, 2017|access-date=March 9, 2017}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2017–2018)=== Evans signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on July 10, 2017.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-tyreke-evans-170710|title=Grizzlies sign Tyreke Evans|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2017|access-date=July 10, 2017}} On November 1 of that year, he led the team with 32 points in a 101–99 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]]; it was his first 30-point performance since December 2014.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974863|title=Fournier scores 22, Gordon adds 19 as Magic beat Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=November 1, 2017|access-date=November 1, 2017}} Midway through the season, Evans filled in for the injured [[Mike Conley Jr.|Mike Conley]] to become the team's starting point guard.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975096|title=Gasol's 21, Evans' free throws help Grizzlies snap skid|work=ESPN.com|date=December 4, 2017|access-date=December 4, 2017}} On December 27, he accumulated 32 points, 7 rebounds, and 7 assists in a 109–99 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975261|title=Evans 32 points lead Grizzlies past Lakers, 109-99|work=ESPN.com|date=December 27, 2017|access-date=December 28, 2017}} After being put on the trade block leading up to the trade deadline, Evans missed time in late January and early February.{{cite web|url=https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2018/2/13/17007256/gbb-roundtable-now-what-for-the-memphis-grizzlies-nba|title=GBB Roundtable: Now what for the Memphis 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220823090701/https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/2018/2/13/17007256/gbb-roundtable-now-what-for-the-memphis-grizzlies-nba|url-status=dead}}{{cite opportunity|work=grizzlybearblues.com|date=February 14, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018}} In his first game back for the Grizzlies on February 11, Evans recorded 12 points and 5 rebounds in a 110–92 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/postgame/okc-180214|title=Postgame Report: Grizzlies come up short against In the contest, Evans went 3 for 7 from outside the arc to make his 28th straight game with at least one 3-pointer, breaking the franchise record of 27 previously held by [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975624|title=James records triple-double as Cavs defeat Grizzlies 112-89|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2018|access-date=February 23, 2018}} On March 15 against the [[Chicago Bulls]], Evans returned to the lineup following a 10-game absence because of a rib injury.{{cite 2018|access-date=March 15, 2018}} ===Indiana Pacers (2018–2019)=== On July 6, 2018, Evans signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-tyreke-evans-doug-mcdermott|title=Pacers Sign Tyreke Evans, Doug McDermott|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}} In the season-opener on October 17, he posted 14 points and 5 assists to debut for his new franchise and help defeat his former team, the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], 111–83.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070695|title=Bogdanovic scores 19 points, Pacers rout Grizzlies 111-83|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}} On November 16, he hit five 3-pointers and scored a season-high 23 points off the bench in a 99–91 win over the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070898|title=Evans scores 23 points to lead Pacers past Heat 99-91|work=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=November 16, 2018}} In game four of the Pacers' first-round playoff series against the [[Boston Celtics]], he scored a playoff career-high 21 points in a 110–106 series-ending loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401126865|title=Celtics complete rare sweep by beating Pacers 110-106|work=ESPN.com|date=April 21, 2019|access-date=April 22, 2019}} ===NBA suspension (2019–2022)=== On May 17, 2019, Evans was [[List of people banned or suspended by the NBA|banned from the NBA]] for violating the terms of its Anti-Drug Program that prohibits [[drug abuse]].{{cite news|last=Owens|first=Jason|title=Tyreke Evans dismissed from NBA for violating league's anti-drug program|date=May 17, 2019|work=Yahoo Sports|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/report-tyreke-evans-dismissed-from-nba-for-violating-leagues-antidrug-program-204850572.html|access-date=May 17, 2019}} He became eligible to apply for reinstatement in 2021,{{cite web |title=Tyreke Evans dismissed from league for violating anti-drug program |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/05/17/tyreke-evans-dismissed-league-official-release |website=NBA.com |access-date=May 17, 2019 |date=May 17, 2019}} and was officially reinstated on February 14, 2022.{{cite web |title=NBA and NBPA reinstate Tyreke Evans |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-nbpa-reinstate-tyreke-evans |website=NBA.com |access-date=15 February 2022 |date=15 February 2022}}
